cf.title: XMLTable treats a column of a domain over xml as a non-xml column

input.subject: XMLTable treats a column of a domain over xml as a non-xml column

verdict_reasoning: No objection to the fix itself survived: looking through domains follows existing practice in XMLTABLE and in map_sql_value_to_xml_value(). The one surviving objection, standards-compat-1, is about the stable target. The patch changes query results and the value a domain CHECK constraint sees, and message #1 does not weigh that for minor releases. A committer decides whether to back-patch or fix master only.

brief.title: Treat domains over xml like xml in XMLTABLE columns
brief.problem: XMLTABLE handles a column declared as a domain over xml like a non-xml column, so a node-set result becomes its string value. In the example, an xml column returns `x` and a domain-over-xml column returns `x`. This affects users who declare XMLTABLE columns with such domains.
brief.proposed_design: XmlTableGetValue() now resolves the column type to its base type with getBaseType() before it tests for XMLOID. A domain over xml then gets the same XML treatment as xml. The patch adds a regression test.
user_visible_surface: XMLTABLE columns of a domain over xml now return the XML node, not its string value.
author_claims: Both columns in the example should return the same value, since the domain is over xml.
XMLTABLE already looks through domains for boolean results, which it maps by type category.
Other code, such as map_sql_value_to_xml_value(), already treats domains like their base types.
The fix belongs in stable branches, as the CommitFest entry targets stable and tags it as a bugfix.
brief.thread_state: Only the first message is visible. No one has replied yet.
unclear: The proposal does not say whether a back-patch is safe, given that existing queries on stable branches would return different results.
The material does not say whether the domain's constraints are still checked on the value it returns.
The material does not say whether other xml functions or the PATH-less default column case have the same typid == XMLOID check.

objections.title: Back-patching changes results of existing XMLTABLE queries in minor releases
objections.failure_scenario: A user has a view or report using XMLTABLE with a domain-over-xml column and gets the string value `x`. After a minor upgrade the same query returns `x`. Downstream code that compares, stores or parses that column breaks, and the user finds out only from wrong output in production.
objections.argument: The CommitFest entry targets stable and is tagged Bugfix, but the patch changes visible query results on stable branches. Message #1 argues the behaviour is inconsistent, yet the current output is well defined and may have users who rely on it. A committer would likely accept the fix for master only and ask for a release-note entry. Domain CHECK constraints now see a different value, so rows that passed before may fail after the upgrade, and the reverse can happen too.
objections.author_must_show: Why should a change in returned values, and in which values domain constraints see, go into minor releases and not only into master with a release note?

critic.reasoning: The CommitFest entry targets stable, and message #1 does not weigh the output change against users of the current result. The domain's input check would receive the node text instead of the string value, so the CHECK constraint point is plausible too.

refuted.title: Back-patching changes results of existing XMLTABLE queries on stable branches
refuted.failure_scenario: A user on a stable branch has a view or report that uses a domain over xml in XMLTABLE and parses the returned string value. After a minor upgrade the column holds `x` instead of `x`. The user finds out when the report or a domain CHECK constraint written for the old value starts to fail.
refuted.argument: The CommitFest entry targets stable and is tagged Bugfix, but message #1 does not say why a silent change in query output is fit for a minor release. The current behaviour is wrong, but it is stable, and some users may depend on it. A committer would likely ask for a master-only fix with a release note, unless the thread shows no one depends on the old output. The fix itself is small and adds no lasting maintenance cost.
refuted.author_must_show: Why is changing XMLTABLE output for domain-over-xml columns in a minor release safer than fixing only master with a release note?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1, which makes the same back-patch point and adds the domain CHECK constraint case.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: The patch changes what an SQL/XML XMLTABLE column of a domain over xml returns.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The CommitFest entry targets stable, and the patch changes results of existing XMLTABLE queries.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: XmlTableGetValue() gains a getBaseType() call when it converts a column value.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Why should a change in XMLTABLE results for domain-over-xml columns go into minor releases, and not only into master with a release note?
Are the domain's CHECK constraints still checked on the returned value, and can a row that passed before the patch now fail?
Do other places in xml.c, such as the column case without PATH, have the same typid == XMLOID test?
Does XmlTableGetValue() call getBaseType() once per column or once per value?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows the XMLTABLE code in xml.c and the back-patch policy for behaviour changes. No one has replied to message #1 yet.
committability.liability: The committer signs for a result change in XMLTABLE on every branch that gets the patch. On stable branches this includes reports from users whose queries or domain constraints relied on the string value.
committability.author_follow_up: No sign either way; the thread has only message #1, posted four days before this review.

priority.reason: The patch is 3.2 KB, touches xml.c and the xml regression test only, and affects only users who declare XMLTABLE columns as domains over xml. The open point is the back-patch decision.

provisional_note: The code was not read. It would show whether domain constraints still run on the returned value, where the getBaseType() call sits, and whether other xml type tests need the same change.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: loop over unbound cursor
precedents_retrieved.summary: Allow the PL/pgSQL FOR loop to iterate over an unbound refcursor that was opened earlier, in addition to bound cursors. If the FOR statement opened the portal itself it closes it at loop end; otherwise iteration continues over the already-open portal, so one cursor can be read across several loops.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane saw no gain over a plain FOR-over-SELECT and thought splitting one iteration across two loops encourages poor programming practice. He also objected that a FOR loop which may or may not own its cursor loses a self-contained definition of its iterations and is no cleaner than a hand-built loop around FETCH. The author replied with use cases (refcursors passed as arguments, symmetry with FETCH, dbms_sql patterns), and the entry was withdrawn with no further messages.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The point of a FOR loop, IMO, is to have a fairly self-contained
definition of the set of iterations that will occur.  This
eliminates that property, leaving you with something no cleaner
than a hand-built loop around a FETCH command.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix standby may crash when switching-over in certain special cases
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes a standby PANIC after switchover, where a failed streaming attempt leaves walrcv->flushedUpto ahead of the WAL actually on disk, so the startup process opens a WAL file that does not exist. It resets walrcv->flushedUpto when streaming is requested again; the revised version does so only when walrcv->receiveStart is greater than the requested location.
precedents_retrieved.objection: No reviewer took up the revised patch. Yugo Nagata objected that the first version re-requests WAL the standby already has, for example under recovery_min_apply_delay. The author revised the patch and in December 2024 posted code to reproduce the crash, but nobody replied, and the visible messages do not say why the entry was withdrawn.

precedents_retrieved.title: iteration over record in plpgsql
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a row_to_array function that turns any row into a text array of field names and values. It also extends plpgsql FOREACH so a list of target variables, such as key and value, can take consecutive elements of an array in one step.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that row_to_array casts all fields to text and drops SQL datatypes, and said row_to_json already covers the case. He also asked that the two features be split and that FOREACH get its own discussion. Jim Nasby worried that the FOREACH pairing rule would block iteration that follows array dimensions. The later messages move to typed iteration over records and broader dynamic typing, and no revised design was agreed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
While I don't have a problem with hstore_to_array, I don't think that
row_to_array is a very good idea; it's basically encouraging people to
throw away SQL datatypes altogether and imagine that everything is text.

precedents_retrieved.title: quick and dirty fix: Quadratic planning time for ordered paths over partitioned tables
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Alvaro Herrera, Aleksander Alekseev
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch caches the position of the last found equivalence member in a static variable in find_ec_member_matching_pathkeys(), so lookups done in partition order take constant time. It was offered as a stopgap for planning time that grows quadratically with the number of partitions, until Yuya Watari's larger equivalence class refactoring lands.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected that one static cache shared by all equivalence classes helps only one call pattern, which unrelated changes could break, and that integer division with a variable divisor may make things slower. He said the fix belongs at a higher level. Alvaro Herrera and Aleksander Alekseev pointed the author to Watari's patch series instead, and Herrera showed it cuts planning time for the same test from about 2700 ms to 600 ms.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
That "quick fix" seems extremely horrid: since there's only one static
cache variable for all ECs, it's going to help only one very specific
call pattern, which could easily get broken by unrelated changes.

precedents_retrieved.title: refactor AlterDomainAddConstraint (alter domain add constraint)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes alter domain ... add constraint reject constraint options that domains do not support (NO INHERIT, NOT ENFORCED, deferrability) with domain-specific error messages. It also removes dead code in AlterDomainAddConstraint().
precedents_retrieved.objection: The visible messages do not show why. Peter Eisentraut committed the dead-code removal, and Alvaro Herrera's last message called the v5 patch a reasonable implementation, ugly though it is, and suggested checking deferrability before calling processCASbits(). No later message appears before the entry was returned with feedback in April 2026.

precedents_retrieved.title: Document AccessExclusive lock behaviour on standbys
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds text to the table-level locks section of the explicit locking documentation. It states that an AccessExclusive lock on the primary is written to WAL and replayed on standbys, so the table is also locked there, and for how long.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add regexp_positions(string text, pattern text, flags text) → setof record (starts integer[], lengths integer[])
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a regexp_positions() function that works like regexp_matches() but returns the positions of matches and capture groups instead of the matched substrings. An earlier int4range[] return type was dropped because empty ranges cannot represent zero-length matches, and the later version returned setof record with parallel arrays of start positions and lengths.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane reviewed the revised patch and raised definitional questions that were still open: whether to add a search-start-position argument, the need for a regexp_match()-style single-result variant, whether separate start and length arrays are confusing, and how sub-matches should be handled. He also listed code and documentation problems. The author did not respond to this review for two months, so the entry was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I am on board now with the general
idea of returning match positions, but I think there are still
definitional issues to be discussed.

precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a list-valued GUC (later named log_connection_messages) that selects which connection stages get logged: received, authenticated, authorized, disconnected, or all. roaster_notes.note: No precedent found. The only retrieved row, [P3], is about domains and polymorphic functions, a different mechanism, and it has no recorded reason that could apply to XMLTABLE column handling. Message #1 does not mention an earlier discussion of this idea. Whether a back-patch is safe, given that existing queries would return different results, is a question for another angle.
The master-only change fits existing practice for looking through domains. The objection is about back-patching only.

The patch changes only how XmlTableGetValue() converts a result at query time, so it adds no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog entry, protocol message or extension API. Already stored data is unaffected, and the behaviour change on stable branches is a back-patch question for other angles.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. It changes how XMLTABLE builds a column value from a document the caller already passes, adds no new access, and widens nothing a user can see. Whether domain CHECK constraints still run on the returned xml value is a data-integrity question for other angles, and the code would show the answer.
From the maintenance angle the fix is small, local to xml.c, and follows existing practice of looking through domains, so it adds no lasting cost. The only concern is the back-patch target.

Users can declare the column as xml and cast it to the domain in the select list, so the result is already reachable. This is a workaround for inconsistent behaviour rather than a competing feature, and no extension covers it, so a committer would not likely reject a small bugfix on these grounds.

This is a small consistency fix, so a demand test is the wrong bar: the cost falls only on users of domains over xml, and the change adds no syntax or GUC. No field report is shown. The workaround of declaring the column as xml exists, and whether a back-patch is safe belongs to another angle.
